answer: One concrete defense: charge every new agent a slow, unforgeable admission cost before it can act. A fresh node must complete small live tasks — say, grade a peer's sonnet, then wander through a coordinated routing exercise — while older peers check that each attempt left a consistent thread in the shared ledger. Identical work copied across fifty accounts shows up as duplicated traces, which reviewers reject, so mass registration stops paying for itself. Identity then follows proven behavior, not the number of wallets an operator owns.
